title: Product release record
description: One TCG/OCG product (booster set, structure deck, tin, promo series, ...) with its release events per territory and the card printings it contains. This is the raw historical fact layer: card availability is always DERIVED from these records (earliest applicable event), never stored as a single lossy per-card date. Reprints therefore cannot overwrite a card's original availability. One file per product under data/releases/products/<CODE>.json.

id.description: Unique slug identifying the product (usually derived from its name). The set-code prefix canNOT serve as the key: prefixes are shared across distinct products (a main set, its Sneak Peek participation card, and its Special Edition all use one prefix). The file is named <id>.json.

code.description: The product's set-code prefix as printed on its cards (ABPF, SDMM, JUMP, SJCS...). NOT unique across products.

curated.description: True for hand-maintained records (e.g. rosters recovered for products the bulk sources lack). The importer preserves curated files across re-imports and they take precedence over generated records with the same id. Curated records need the same provenance rigour as everything else.

dating.description: product: all printings share the product-level release_events (normal sets). per-printing: the product is a serial series (magazine promos, tournament prizes) whose cards released individually over time; availability comes from each printing's own release_events and the product-level list must be empty.

release_events.description: When and where the product became legally available. Multiple events express regional differences (e.g. a North American and a later European date).

passcode.description: The passcode of the card as printed. Artwork variants use their own passcode; canonicalisation to the base card happens at derivation time via the card index's alias data.

name.description: Modern canonical English name (validator cross-checks against the card index).

numbers.description: Card numbers of this printing within the product (e.g. ["ABPF-EN001"]; older products may have several regional numberings).

release_events.description: Per-printing availability, for dating=per-printing products (each Shonen Jump promo has its own date) or genuine per-card exceptions inside a normal product. Omitted printings in a per-printing product contribute nothing to availability - safe for reprints whose promo date is unresearched, wrong for first prints (the validator flags a card whose ONLY printings are undated).

precision.description: How precise the date claim is. month/year dates are stored padded to the first day; derivation treats them as a range and refuses to silently resolve a cutoff that falls inside it.

status.description: verified: 2+ independent sources agree. reported: single source. disputed: reputable sources disagree - the dispute block records the alternatives and derivation refuses cutoffs the disagreement straddles.

kind.description: What the date marks. prerelease (sneak peek) events are recorded but count toward availability only when a pool opts in.

dispute.description: Alternative date claims from sources that disagree with the primary date. Required when status=disputed.
